fixes.explanation: Yes, that's the one. God says He will send fire on Magog and on those in the coastlands, “…and they will know that I am the LORD.” That's how the verse ends. It says it plainly, with no fancy words.

Yes, friend, burning them is the answer. God says those who dwell in the cities of Israel will go out, kindle fires and burn up the weapons. “For seven years they will use them for fuel.” Everything from the bucklers and shields to the clubs and spears goes into the fire (Ezekiel 39:9).
Nope, there's no stockpile here. God says the people will go out, kindle fires and burn the weapons. “For seven years they will use them for fuel.” The weapons are fuel, not a stash for battle.

Yes, and what a turnaround, friend. God says they “…will loot those who looted them and plunder those who plundered them, declares the Lord GOD.” The ones who did the taking become the ones taken from.

Achor is a real valley, but it belongs to a different story. It shows up in Joshua 7:24-26, where Israel took Achan, a man of Israel, to that valley. In this passage, God says the valley where Gog and his hordes are buried will be called Hamon-gog (Ezekiel 39:11). Same Bible, different valley.

That's the word. God says, “For seven months the house of Israel will be burying them in order to cleanse the land.” He uses it again in verse 16: “…And so they will cleanse the land.” And at the end of the seven months, they begin a search for the invaders who remain on the ground (Ezekiel 39:14).

Yes, friend. God says the one who sees a human bone “…will set up a pillar next to it, until the gravediggers have buried it in the Valley of Hamon-gog.” The pillar marks the spot. The burying ends up with the gravediggers, in the valley.

Not this time, friend. God is the one speaking, and He says the house of Israel “…were unfaithful to Me. So I hid My face from them…” So True is the answer. It's a heavy part of the passage, and it's right there in Ezekiel 39:23.

That's not what God says. He says, “Now I will restore Jacob from captivity and will have compassion on the whole house of Israel…” Magog is where He says He'll send fire (Ezekiel 39:6). Giving Israel that land isn't a promise in this verse.

That one sounds like a bad habit, friend. But the verse says something different. God says, “They will forget their disgrace and all the treachery they committed against Me…” The word is forget, and it comes when they dwell securely in their land.

Yes. God says, “When I bring them back from the peoples and gather them out of the lands of their enemies, I will show My holiness in them in the sight of many nations.” Notice who does the showing: God says, “I will show My holiness in them.” It's His holiness, and many nations see it in His people.

That's the word. God says, “And I will no longer hide My face from them, for I will pour out My Spirit on the house of Israel, declares the Lord GOD.” I think it's a good place to land, because the passage ends with His face no longer hidden.
